title: Banned JAAC Calls Region-Wide Shutter-Down Strike Across Azad Kashmir; Government and Activists Give Conflicting Accounts
detail: The banned Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) called a region-wide shutter-down and wheel-jam strike across Pakistan-administered Azad Jammu & Kashmir (AJK) on September 9, 2026, demanding full implementation of the October 2025 reforms agreement and renewing calls for the group's proscription to be lifted, the release of detained activists, and an independent judicial inquiry into the June 2026 crackdown violence. Accounts of the strike's impact diverged sharply along political lines. The AJK government and the Express Tribune reported the strike as a widespread failure, with markets, shops and public transport operating normally in Mirpur, Muzaffarabad, Kotli and Bhimber, and cited statements from Mirpur's business community thanking the administration and police for maintaining law and order. Independent outlet Waging Nonviolence, reporting on the broader JAAC movement's resilience, described the September 9 action as a general strike with protesters remaining in the streets despite the crackdown, and noted that internet access remains completely suspended in Rawalakot and Sudhnoti months after the unrest began, with dozens still under arrest and precise casualty figures unclear due to restricted media access. The action follows a summer of unrest in which, per JKHRO's running tally, at least 89 people have been killed since protests began June 7, 2026, including student organiser Usama Jamil, shot by security forces on July 27 in Rawalakot, and activist Shahzaib Habib, killed by unidentified men on June 6.

confidenceReason: That JAAC called a September 9 shutdown and that AJK authorities mobilized to counter it is confirmed by both a pro-state Tier-2 outlet and an independent Tier-3 outlet; the degree of public participation and whether the strike succeeded or failed is sharply disputed between government-aligned and activist/independent reporting.

title: PM Shehbaz Sharif Holds First Meeting With New AJK PM Iftikhar Gilani, Pledges Federal Support
detail: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met newly-elected Azad Jammu & Kashmir Prime Minister Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gilani at the PM House in Islamabad on September 9, 2026 — their first meeting since Gilani's contested August 28 election as AJK's 17th premier. The two discussed peace and development in AJK and ongoing federal welfare projects in the region. Sharif said the federal government 'will continue to take all possible measures for the development and prosperity of the people of Azad Jammu and Kashmir,' while Gilani said he would 'utilise all his capabilities for the development of the region and the welfare of its people.' The meeting comes amid continuing JAAC-led unrest in AJK and follows the September 4 swearing-in of Gilani's eight-member cabinet; no mention was made publicly of the ongoing protest movement or JKHRO's casualty tally from the summer crackdown.
